title: Redefining "Basic Needs" in Social Policies Given Need to Foster Sense of Belonging, Income Inequality Gap and Other Challenges
what_it_is: Redefining "Basic Needs" in Social Policies Given Need to Foster Sense of Belonging, Income Inequality Gap and Other Challenges

sections.label: Basic needs and ComCare support
sections.summary: Basic needs include biological, physical and socio-psychological needs, and ComCare helps lower-income families meet basic living expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Basic needs comprise not just biological and physical necessities like food, shelter and transport, but also socio-psychological needs, such as social connections and emotional support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Government works with the community to provide multiple lines of support to families who have difficulty meeting these needs on their own.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: ComCare helps lower-income families to meet their basic living expenses.

sections.label: Mobile data under ComCare
sections.summary: Mobile data plans are now covered under ComCare assistance because digital connectivity is recognised as a basic need today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: As an example of how the ComCare scheme has evolved over time, mobile data plans are now covered under ComCare assistance as we recognise that digital connectivity, which in turn enables human connection, is a basic need in modern society today.

sections.label: Income inequality and ComLink
sections.summary: Addressing income inequality means providing opportunity, and ComLink helps lower-income families in public rental housing through customised action plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Ultimately, addressing income inequality is not just about shoring up basic needs, but about providing opportunity and seeking to level the playing field for those who face disadvantages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: This is why we have introduced initiatives, such as Community Link (ComLink) for lower-income families with children living in public rental housing, to proactively identify their needs, journey with them on customised action plans to secure a better future for them.

sections.label: Reviewing support for families
sections.summary: The last review was in August 2022, and a basket of needs is reviewed periodically to address cost-of-living pressures on families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The last review that we have done was in August 2022 and the Member would agree that with the recent pressures on cost-of-living, we need to be adept and prompt in addressing the needs of these families because oftentimes, those that are in these families are hardest hit by cost of living pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In terms of how we review what is to be included and at what level do we provide support for these families, we do look at a basket of needs that get reviewed from time to time, periodically – as I have mentioned in my main reply.
